item.title: South Carolina's measles outbreak nears 790 cases — making it the biggest in decades
item.description: Nearly 790 people, primarily children, have been infected in South Carolina's ongoing measles outbreak, officials report.

item.title: James Webb telescope discovers closest galaxy to the Big Bang ever seen
item.description: The James Webb Space Telescope has confirmed the most distant, early galaxy in the known universe. The new contender, MoM-z14, is visible just 280 million years after the Big Bang.

item.title: Halley wasn't the first to figure out the famous comet. An 11th-century monk did it first, new research suggests.
item.description: An 11th-century monk saw the famous "Halley's comet" first as a child and later as an adult, new research finds.

item.title: The Snow Moon will 'swallow' one of the brightest stars in the sky this weekend: Where and when to look
item.description: On the night of Feb. 2, skywatchers in eastern North America can see the moon occult Regulus — a rare event visible to the naked eye.

item.title: Hawke Frontier ED X 8x42 review
item.description: An award-winning birding binocular with both style and substance at a reasonable price — a must for any nature enthusiast.

item.title: Watch awkward Chinese humanoid robot lay it all down on the dance floor
item.description: The model demonstrated remarkable precision, stability and speed across a highly complex dance routine.

item.title: More than 43,000 years ago, Neanderthals spent centuries collecting animal skulls in a cave; but archaeologists aren't sure why
item.description: Neanderthals repeatedly returned to the cave to store horned animal skulls, revealing this cultural tradition was transmitted over time.

item.title: 'Part of the evolutionary fabric of our societies': Same-sex sexual behavior in primates may be a survival strategy, study finds
item.description: A new study comparing 59 species of primates linked same-sex sexual behavior to scarce resources and more predators in socially complex species. The findings show diverse sexual behaviors are common — and likely beneficial in primates.

item.title: Thousands of dams in the US are old, damaged and unable to cope with extreme weather. How bad is it?
item.description: Dams in the U.S. are showing signs of damage that are worsening with age and climate change. Could satellites help prioritize repairs amid budget and inspection constraints?

item.title: New triple-drug treatment stops pancreatic cancer in its tracks, a mouse study finds
item.description: By targeting three key growth pathways at once, researchers eliminated pancreatic tumors in multiple mouse models and prevented the cancer from returning, a promising step toward overcoming treatment resistance.
